section_summary: These pages trace negotiations in 1936 over Japan’s requirement that oil companies hold six months’ stocks. Standard-Vacuum and Rising Sun sought an arrangement with Mitsui that would shift non-commercial storage to Japanese interests while preserving their share of the market. Embassy reports, company cables, memoranda and press coverage record disagreements over the arrangement, its cost and where negotiations should take place.

subfiles.title: Notes on discussion with Yoshino and Kurusu
subfiles.about: Foreign oil representatives discuss a possible Mitsui arrangement and relief from stockholding rules.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino and Kurusu welcome an approach to Mitsui, while suggesting other Japanese partners might also be considered. Yoshino promises continued trade quotas but gives no official undertaking to suspend the law.

subfiles.title: Conversation at Mitsui Gomei Kaisha
subfiles.about: Foreign oil representatives propose talks with Mitsui on oil stocks and a wider commercial arrangement.
subfiles.summary: Ely and Meyer explain their companies’ objection to setting a precedent for non-commercial stocks and seek a conference in New York. Nanjo and Tajima discuss possible arrangements, including a joint company, but question the venue and ask for time to consult Mukai.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding despatch No. 1757
subfiles.about: Forwards Tokyo’s April 1 despatch on Japan’s oil situation.
subfiles.summary: Encloses despatch No. 1757 and its enclosures.

subfiles.title: Parker letter enclosing an oil-controversy article
subfiles.about: Asks Hornbeck to comment on a newspaper story about the oil dispute.
subfiles.summary: Parker encloses the article and requests information or comment.

subfiles.title: U.S. and British oil firms may withdraw from Japanese market
subfiles.about: Claims Japan’s oil law may force American and British companies to withdraw.
subfiles.summary: The article describes storage requirements, diplomatic protests and possible alternative Japanese fuel supplies.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck acknowledgment of Parker’s article
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Parker’s clipping and promises an account of its origins.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Parker and says he will send facts and his opinion.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck explanation of the oil article
subfiles.about: Explains how a sensational oil story arose and describes the Department’s publicity policy.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck traces the story to a public congressional hearing and subsequent inquiries by its author. He says the Department did not supply the article’s sensational claims and intends to avoid publicity while negotiations continue.

subfiles.title: Oil showdown with Japan due soon
subfiles.about: Condenses claims that the oil law may trigger a confrontation with foreign companies.
subfiles.summary: Reports storage requirements and a possible American and British withdrawal.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck letter enclosing Far Eastern Survey article
subfiles.about: Sends another article on Japan’s oil dispute to Parker.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck notes that the Institute of Pacific Relations had not requested information from the Department.

subfiles.title: Foreign oil companies in Japan face impasse
subfiles.about: Surveys the storage dispute, marketing quotas and Japan’s search for oil.
subfiles.summary: The article describes the stalemate over six-month stocks, quotas favoring Japanese companies, and exploration in Timor, Borneo, the Netherlands Indies and North Sakhalin.

subfiles.title: Parker letter endorsing limited publicity
subfiles.about: Agrees that publicity should be avoided during negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Parker recalls the companies’ earlier agreement with Japan to refrain from press statements.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 1800
subfiles.about: Recommends reading the Embassy’s oil despatch.
subfiles.summary: Says the despatch outlines its two long conversation memoranda.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1800: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Mitsui’s response and Yoshino’s wish for a definite proposal.
subfiles.summary: Mitsui declines a storage-only role but is willing to discuss a wider trading arrangement in Tokyo. Yoshino urges the companies to formulate a proposal quickly.

subfiles.title: Mukai letter declining oil-storage proposal
subfiles.about: Declines the proposal presented to Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: Mukai says Mitsui cannot entertain the storage proposal and offers a later explanation.

subfiles.title: Conversation at Mitsui Bussan Kaisha
subfiles.about: Discusses the scope and location of possible Mitsui negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Mukai and Tajima reject a warehousing role but express interest in trading. They insist on talks in Tokyo and ask the companies to present a clearer proposal.

subfiles.title: Meeting with Vice Minister Yoshino
subfiles.about: Yoshino presses the oil companies to advance their talks with Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino describes pressure to approve expanded Japanese refining capacity and concern about delay. He suggests government encouragement might make Mitsui more willing to negotiate.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding despatch No. 1800
subfiles.about: Forwards Tokyo’s May 1 despatch and enclosures.
subfiles.summary: Sends despatch No. 1800 for the ambassador’s information.

subfiles.title: Parker letter on the Far Eastern Survey source
subfiles.about: Reports Parker’s inquiries into the source of a periodical article.
subfiles.summary: Parker says Catherine Porter drew on publications and at least one oil-company interview.

subfiles.title: Division note on hydrogenation talks
subfiles.about: Summarizes a consul’s report of possible hydrogenation-plant negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Suggests the talks may relate to the broader oil dispute.

subfiles.title: Consular despatch on hydrogenation in Japan
subfiles.from: Richard F. Boyce, American Consul, Yokohama
subfiles.about: Reports on Joseph Wilhelm Faessler and possible coal-hydrogenation plants in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Boyce describes Faessler’s work with Ahrens and I. G. Farben and the oil companies’ interest in relevant patent rights. He considers the process potentially available to Japan after an oil agreement and requests technical information.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck routing note to Phillips
subfiles.about: Directs Phillips to portions of a despatch.
subfiles.summary: Recommends reading the end of page four and most of page five.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 1860
subfiles.about: Recommends reading Tokyo’s report on oil negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Highlights Yoshino’s wish that the foreign companies stay and Mitsui avoid further delay.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1860: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports a new foreign-company proposal, Japanese responses and possible alternative storage arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The companies propose that Mitsui carry non-commercial stocks in return for government compensation and a share of the oil business. Yoshino wants progress before July 1, while Mitsui stresses the difficulty of coordinating ministries and disputes the proposed New York venue. The despatch also notes reports of a semi-official storage company and increased subsidies for oil exploration.

subfiles.title: New York cable outlining proposed Mitsui arrangement
subfiles.about: Sets out terms for transferring non-commercial stocks to Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: The plan offers Mitsui compensation, supply contracts and a share of trade, while seeking percentage quotas throughout Japan’s market. It warns that without such an arrangement the companies may withdraw.

subfiles.title: Interview at the Department of Commerce and Industry
subfiles.about: Ely and Meyer present their headquarters’ Mitsui proposal to Yoshino.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino says the government wants the foreign companies to remain in Japan. He urges prompt discussion with Mitsui and hopes the principles of an arrangement can be settled before July 1.

subfiles.title: Meeting at Mitsui Bussan Kaisha
subfiles.about: Ely and Meyer present the revised proposal to Mukai.
subfiles.summary: Mukai calls it reasonable but reserves Mitsui’s response pending study.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding despatch No. 1860
subfiles.to: American Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, London
subfiles.about: Forwards Tokyo’s May 27 oil despatch.
subfiles.summary: Encloses despatch No. 1860 and its enclosures.

subfiles.title: Parker letter about Kurusu’s visit
subfiles.about: Provides company cables before Kurusu’s Washington visit.
subfiles.summary: Parker asks to hear of developments bearing on the oil dispute before meeting Kurusu.

subfiles.title: Company cable from New York to Yokohama
subfiles.about: Repeats headquarters’ proposed arrangement with Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: Proposes Japanese stockholding, compensation and trade relations, together with percentage quotas for the foreign companies.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cable reporting Mitsui’s counterproposal
subfiles.about: Reports Mitsui’s ideas for a Japanese-capitalized oil company.
subfiles.summary: Mitsui refuses New York talks and suggests a new company to import and hold stocks, with income from compensation, storage fees and trade. The Yokohama representatives discuss capital needs, returns and how to limit the foreign companies’ costs.

subfiles.title: New York cable seeking tariff and subsidy information
subfiles.about: Asks about the revised tariff, storage subsidy and a possible stockholding maximum.
subfiles.summary: Requests the status and likely timing of those measures.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cable answering tariff and subsidy questions
subfiles.about: Reports enactment of the tariff and subsidy and uncertainty about stock limits.
subfiles.summary: Says the tariff and ¥2,640,000 subsidy passed, while future compensation and stockholding rules remain uncertain.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding Parker conversation memorandum to London
subfiles.to: American Chargé d’Affaires ad interim, London
subfiles.about: Forwards a June 11 conversation memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Sends the memorandum concerning Parker, Kurusu and the oil dispute.

subfiles.title: Telephone conversation with Parker about Kurusu
subfiles.about: Relates the Department’s discussion with Kurusu and Parker’s response.
subfiles.summary: Dooman tells Parker that officials expressed dissatisfaction to Kurusu over Japan’s treatment of American oil interests. Parker disputes Kurusu’s account of guaranteed sales, stressing the companies’ wish to share in market growth. He asks that Kurusu urge Mitsui to send negotiators to New York before the stockholding deadline.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding Parker conversation memorandum to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards the June 11 conversation memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Sends the Parker-Kurusu oil discussion for the ambassador’s information.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram No. 137 on stockholding assurance
subfiles.about: Reports Yoshino’s minimum acceptable assurance from the foreign oil companies.
subfiles.summary: Yoshino seeks a statement that an arrangement to meet legal stockholding obligations has been agreed in principle. Grew reports that further postponement of enforcement is unlikely.

subfiles.title: Division note on despatch No. 1895
subfiles.about: Assesses Mitsui’s tentative terms and awaits further reports.
subfiles.summary: The note says a settlement has been reported in the press and anticipates details, including analysis of revised petroleum tariffs.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1895: American oil interests in Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Details Mitsui’s proposed storage company and Japanese government pressure for progress.
subfiles.summary: Mitsui proposes a Japanese-capitalized company funded by government compensation, storage fees and a share of petroleum trade, while insisting that talks remain outside New York. The companies are still considering the commercial terms. Japanese officials request assurance of progress before assigning new quotas; Grew also reports the revised import tariffs and approved storage compensation.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding despatch No. 1895
subfiles.about: Forwards Tokyo’s June 12 despatch.
subfiles.summary: Encloses despatch No. 1895 on American oil interests in Japan.

subfiles.title: Document file note for despatch No. 1829
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report on recent oil developments.
subfiles.summary: Points to despatch No. 1829 on American oil interests in Japan.

subfiles.title: American oil interests: Mitsui response
subfiles.about: Summarizes Mitsui’s response to the foreign oil companies’ proposal.
subfiles.summary: Mitsui rejects a storage-only role but invites a definite proposal involving trade.

subfiles.title: Document file note for despatch No. 1882
subfiles.about: Cross-references a report on the plan presented to Yoshino.
subfiles.summary: Points to despatch No. 1882 about the May 16 oil-company proposal.
